steps.what: Locate specifications matching the machine model and revision
Read blueprints, charts and schematics to determine settings or adjustments

tasks.design: Configure model and revision filters in {DOCS} to narrow specification lookup. The technician still reads the relevant diagrams and decides which settings apply; no model interprets a schematic on their behalf.
tasks.previous_blocker: Documents for similar models and revisions are mixed together.
tasks.enabler_now: Native metadata filters can reduce document hunting without interpreting technical meaning.
tasks.still_hard: Determining applicability to modified equipment and actual faults.
tasks.human_edge: The technician relates the drawing to the machine in front of them.
tasks.altitude: Less document hunting with unchanged technical judgement.

evidence.claim: Document metadata filters can reduce lookup where manufacturer and revision fields are reliable; technical interpretation stays human. This is an E1 design estimate.

assumptions: Boundary covers locating and reading specifications, excluding physically changing and testing the equipment.

Manufacturer produces model, document revision and applicability in existing manuals; technician reads the machine model, serial range and installed revision during s1. Its remaining 18 hours include lookup-key capture and manual search when metadata is missing.
Additional metadata correction costs three focal hours and two document-administrator hours per 100 baseline hours; no perfectly indexed library is presumed.
Test native document search and filters before custom code. No saving is assigned to existing search runtime.
research_questions: Do model and revision filters save time after machine identification and missing-document fallback?

already_counted.description: Identify machine and handle ambiguous document matches

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=18+70=88; gross 12 minus 3 upkeep gives net 9. Low 2 allows seven extra lookup hours for modified machines. Specification interpretation remains at full time; E1.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Train new repairers through demonstration, supervised practice and feedback

tasks.design: Retain practical instruction, observation and feedback by the experienced technician. Existing procedures in {DOCS} can support learning without replacing supervised repair practice.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repair competence requires physical practice and judgement.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable instructions support consistency but do not establish shorter supervision.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising unsafe habits and adapting instruction to a new repairer's skill.
tasks.human_edge: The trainer observes technique and intervenes at the right moment.
tasks.altitude: Training time and competence responsibility stay unchanged.

reach.task: Plan supervised practice for new repairers

evidence.claim: Practical repair training depends on demonstration, supervision and feedback; digital instructions alone do not replace those activities.

assumptions: Boundary is direct practical training; separate course administration and content creation are not added as a baseline.
Trainer observes trainee performance during the full-time step; no free structured competency assessment is assumed.
Review existing training procedures before creating tools.
Zero incremental upkeep because the training workflow is unchanged; trainee time remains outside the trainer's denominator and is not reduced.
research_questions: Which current training operations are separate administration rather than practical teaching?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; net 0. Supervised practice and human feedback are unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Copy component programs and maintain schematics

steps.what: Identify source programs, target components and schematic revisions
Enter parameters to copy programs between electronic components
Draw, modify and store schematics to reflect equipment changes
Check copied programs and schematic revisions against the repair instruction

tasks.design: Configure saved transfer profiles in {OTHER}, the approved component programming tool, for repeated compatible transfers. The technician binds each profile to the exact source and target before execution, retains schematic editing and checks the resulting files and equipment.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated transfers can require manual parameter entry.
tasks.enabler_now: Native profiles can reuse checked settings without generating new program logic.
tasks.still_hard: Component compatibility and whether a schematic accurately reflects the actual equipment.
tasks.human_edge: The technician validates applicability and recognises incorrect but syntactically valid results.
tasks.altitude: Less repetitive transfer entry with unchanged technical decisions and schematic work.

evidence.claim: Saved programming profiles can remove repeated parameter entry for compatible components; this does not automate schematic design or count machine transfer runtime as labour.

assumptions: Boundary is operator information entry, program copying and schematic editing, excluding broader repair labour. Shares represent a mixed task portfolio; customers must confirm the copying versus drawing mix.

Technician produces source file identifier and checksum, target component identifier, model/revision compatibility, transfer mode and backup reference in s1. Its full 30 hours include capture, backup selection and approval of the exact transfer. Missing compatibility evidence requires manual handling rather than profile execution.
s2 removes only repeated manual parameter entry; existing copy runtime earns no saving. Schematic drawing and modification remain entirely human in s3.
Test native supported transfer profiles before custom code. Four focal hours maintain compatibility tests and two other-role support hours maintain approved profiles per 100 baseline hours.
research_questions: Can saved profiles remove repeated entry after exact source/target approval and result verification?

already_counted.description: Capture and approve exact transfer parameters

approvals.approved_version: Exact source checksum, target component identifier, compatibility revision, transfer mode and backup reference captured and approved in s1; any change prevents execution until reapproved

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=30+0+35+15=80; gross 20 less 4 upkeep gives net 16. Low 3 allows 13 extra hours for nonstandard transfers. Schematic design, compatibility checks and final testing retain time; E1.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Reduce document hunting and repeated transfer entry while preserving technical interpretation and hands-on teaching.
reach: Help electronics repairers check revision compatibility
role.ambitious_version: A repair technician who finds the right specification quickly and executes repeatable transfers with explicit source and target checks.
